class_name: 限定-そのもの-ニカギッテ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

patterns.usage_note: Two jobs share one form. In announcements and signage the polite に限り and に限って simply fence something off as the sole case that qualifies (本日に限り, 会員の方に限り); before a noun this becomes 〜に限っての (本日に限っての特別価格, 今回に限っての措置). に限り fences a case off as the qualifying condition in official notices, where だけ and のみ merely count; and unlike だけ, に限って carries the exasperated on-that-one-occasion reading, naming the single time things perversely go wrong. A matching variant, 〜に限って〜ない, voices the speaker's refusal to believe ill of someone they trust; it states conviction rather than fact, and the うちの子に限って speaker is famously often wrong. It attaches to a noun, so a time span needs a noun head like 日 or 時 to hang on.

examples.ruby: 本日[ほんじつ]に限[かぎ]っての特別価格[とくべつかかく]ですので、お早[はや]めにどうぞ。
examples.english: This is a today-only price, so don't wait.

examples.ruby: 急[いそ]いでいる朝[あさ]に限[かぎ]って、電車[でんしゃ]が遅[おく]れる。
examples.english: The train runs late precisely on the mornings I'm in a hurry.

examples.ruby: うちの子[こ]に限[かぎ]って、そんなことをするはずがない。
examples.english: Not my child. There's no way he'd do a thing like that.
